case_title: Ex-Gunner Virender Prasad v. Union of India & Anr.
accused_occupation: Gunner (soldier) in the Signals Corps, Indian Army
accused_victim_relationship: Co-worker (same army unit); described as on good terms
statutory_provisions: Army Act 1950 s.69 (civil offence of murder, contrary to Ranbir Penal Code s.302)
evidence_type: Oral testimony of 15 witnesses including a psychiatrist; the judgment does not detail the other evidence
confession: Extra-judicial confession to senior authorities after surrender; the Supreme Court did not expressly rely on it
aggravating_circumstances: Victim shot while asleep; a complete magazine of rifle ammunition was fired
mitigating_circumstances: Posted in Kashmir when terrorism was at its peak; immediate surrender and explanation of delusion; excellent jail conduct
trial_court_outcome: Court martial: guilty of murder; life imprisonment and dismissal from service
high_court_outcome: No High Court decision; the Delhi High Court writ petition was transferred to the Armed Forces Tribunal, which dismissed the appeal
offence_finally_established: Murder (civil offence under Army Act s.69)
neutral_facts: The accused was a gunner in a signals corps unit and was posted to a radar post, having reported there in May 2003. The victim, a radar operator from the same regiment, was on good terms with the accused. On the date of the incident the accused shot the victim while the victim was asleep. The accused said the shooting happened in the belief that a militant attack was under way and that he had no control over his senses at the time. A complete magazine of rifle ammunition was fired, and the victim died as a result. Immediately afterwards the accused came out of the tent, surrendered to senior authorities and confessed guilt. Police registered a case and submitted a challan, but at the request of army authorities the case, the challan and the seized items were handed over to the army for trial. Fifteen witnesses, including a psychiatrist, were examined.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from gunshot wounds
premeditation_planning: Not found; the judgment does not address premeditation. The accused's account was that he acted in a delusion.
key_evidence_accepted: The Court Martial's findings of fact, as confirmed by the Armed Forces Tribunal, including the finding of guilt for murder
post_offence_conduct: Came out of the tent, surrendered to senior authorities, confessed guilt and explained the delusion
custody_duration: 16 years and 6 months as on 6.1.2020 (the Court notes that with remission the period would be 20 years and 5 months)
trial_duration: offence: 30.06.2003; trial judgment: 21.08.2004 (court martial order); High Court: not given (Armed Forces Tribunal order dated 16.02.2012); Supreme Court: 18.03.2020
legal_representation: Accused: B.K. Pal (with others on the record). Union of India: Vikramjit Banerjee, Additional Solicitor General
investigation_status: FIR registered and challan submitted; case then handed over to Army authorities for court martial trial
appeal_history: Trial (court martial): guilty of murder, life imprisonment. Petition to Ministry of Defence/Chief of Army Staff dismissed 22.05.2007. Armed Forces Tribunal dismissed the appeal (16.02.2012). Supreme Court: conviction affirmed, sentence reduced to period already undergone.
defence_argument: Not stated for the Supreme Court hearing; the accused's position was that he fired in a delusion of a militant attack and had no control over his senses
legal_principle_applied: Sentence must be proportionate, weighing the Santa Singh factors; s.433-A Cr.P.C. applies to s.69 Army Act cases (14 years' actual imprisonment before release)
precedent_relied_upon: Santa Singh v. State of Punjab (1976) 4 SCC 190; Gopal Singh v. State of Uttarakhand (2013) 7 SCC 545; Union of India v. Sadha Singh (1999) 8 SCC 375
sentencing_rationale: Sentence already served is much more than proportionate to the offence, given the circumstances, surrender, excellent jail conduct and more than 14 years served
judicial_mitigating_factors: Posted in Kashmir when terrorism was at its peak; immediate surrender and explanation of delusion; excellent conduct in jail; more than 14 years served
other_sentence_order: Appellant to be released forthwith from custody
